+[package]
+name = "camcraft-ui-kit"
+description = "Design system of the camcraft shell: theme tokens, theme files, contrast checks, gallery."
+version.workspace = true
+edition.workspace = true
+rust-version.workspace = true
+
+# #4394: egui and serde_json only - no camcraft crate, no flecs, no engine.
+# The kit cannot see the document; that is the point of the crate.
+[dependencies]
+egui = { workspace = true }
+# The camcraft-theme/1 reader walks serde_json Values directly (M6.1 B).
+serde_json = { workspace = true }
+# The gallery window only (feature `gallery`): `cargo test -p camcraft-ui-kit`
+# builds no windowing stack. eframe is already in the lock (egui_kittest,
+# the wasm shell). winit is named only for its default features (x11 and
+# wayland, as camcraft-ui has them): eframe turns them off, and a Linux
+# window needs one. Both crates are already in the lock - no new crate.
+eframe = { workspace = true, optional = true }
+winit = { workspace = true, optional = true }
+
+[features]
+gallery = ["dep:eframe", "dep:winit"]
+
+[[bin]]
+name = "ui-kit-gallery"
+path = "src/bin/ui-kit-gallery.rs"
+required-features = ["gallery"]

+//! camcraft-ui-kit: the design system of the camcraft shell (#4394, step 0
+//! of the #4245 plan) - the theme token table and its clamps, the
+//! `camcraft-theme/1` file reader, the contrast arithmetic and its
+//! readability gate, and a gallery that shows them. The crate depends on
+//! egui and serde_json only: it cannot see the document, so a component
+//! here takes plain data and returns the user's choice, and `camcraft-ui`
+//! turns that choice into an undoable command.
+//! Provenance: our own crate, split out of `camcraft-ui` at the
+//! maintainer's direction (#4245); no HSMWorks material.
+
+pub mod contrast;
+pub mod gallery;
+pub mod theme;
+pub mod theme_files;

+//! The theme's single token table (M6.1 A): every colour, radius, spacing
+//! and size the shell shows is a named field here - widget path and
+//! painted path read the SAME struct, so a retheme is one table and the
+//! two render paths cannot drift. The law is adopted from a sibling
+//! project's proven design at the user's direction (ROADMAP M6.1); the
+//! values are ours - the dark column carries today's `Palette::DARK`
+//! numbers verbatim so the snapshots stay meaningful through the change.
+//!
+//! The drift guard is structural, not a checklist: the const block below
+//! destructures EVERY `Tokens` field without a `..` arm, so adding a
+//! field without wiring it (or explicitly resting it in the painted
+//! path) fails to build - the sibling repo's exhaustiveness pattern,
+//! restated for a table that paints as well as widgets.
+//! Since #4394 the table lives in the `camcraft-ui-kit` crate; the
+//! process-wide live table (`current`, `set_current`, `apply`) stays in
+//! `camcraft-ui`, which owns the running shell.
+//! Provenance: our own module (graduated from the spike and the M6.1 A
+//! rework), specced from the imgui theme we already ship, the egui
+//! Visuals docs, and the sibling architecture at the user's direction;
+//! no HSMWorks material.
+
+use egui::{Color32, CornerRadius, Margin, Stroke, Style, Visuals, vec2};
+
+use crate::contrast;
+
+pub mod clamp;
+mod dropdown;
+mod legal;
+mod tables;
+pub use dropdown::DropGeom;
+
+/// One theme's whole truth: colours, then geometry.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct Tokens {
+    // -- colours: the old Palette, names unchanged (M6.1 B keys on them).
+    /// Window/panel ground.
+    pub ink: Color32,
+    /// Ribbon / browser / header ground (one step above ink).
+    pub ink_alt: Color32,
+    /// Input fields and empty recesses (one step below ink).
+    pub well: Color32,
+    pub text: Color32,
+    pub text_dim: Color32,
+    pub text_faint: Color32,
+    pub border: Color32,
+    /// The selection/hover accent (steel blue).
+    pub accent: Color32,
+    pub accent_hover: Color32,
+    /// Widget-field ground, by interaction state.
+    pub field_bg: Color32,
+    pub field_hover: Color32,
+    pub field_active: Color32,
+    /// Text selection and combo-open highlight.
+    pub selection_bg: Color32,
+    pub selection_stroke: Color32,
+    /// The viewport's 3D ground (the render pass clear colour).
+    pub viewport: Color32,
+    /// Ink of a plain ribbon glyph, read against `strip_fill` (#2021).
+    pub ribbon_ink: Color32,
+    /// Viewport handles (#1120): the shadow under a move or turn handle,
+    /// its readout and the origin triads, and the readout text over the
+    /// viewport.
+    pub handle_shade: Color32,
+    pub handle_text: Color32,
+    /// Rim of a picked point's disc in the viewport (#1120).
+    pub pick_rim: Color32,
+    /// The viewport furniture (#1120): view cube, nav buttons, corner
+    /// hint, playback marker, axis triad and the hover gold. Each table
+    /// holds the set for its own viewport ground; a theme file that turns
+    /// the ground light or dark gets the matching set (`theme_files`).
+    pub cube_edge: Color32,
+    pub cube_label: Color32,
+    pub cube_glyph_on: Color32,
+    pub cube_glyph_off: Color32,
+    pub viewport_hint: Color32,
+    pub marker_stem: Color32,
+    pub marker_ring: Color32,
+    pub marker_dot: Color32,
+    pub axis_x: Color32,
+    pub axis_y: Color32,
+    pub axis_z: Color32,
+    pub viewport_hover: Color32,
+    /// The viewport overlays (#1120): the generate progress panel, the
+    /// file drop hint, the empty-view text, the pick halo, the fixture
+    /// plate marks and the selected G-code move. Both tables hold the
+    /// values the draw sites wrote before.
+    pub overlay_panel: Color32,
+    pub overlay_edge: Color32,
+    pub overlay_text: Color32,
+    pub overlay_track: Color32,
+    pub drop_veil: Color32,
+    pub empty_hint: Color32,
+    pub pick_halo: Color32,
+    pub plate_hole: Color32,
+    pub plate_dowel: Color32,
+    pub gcode_line: Color32,
+    /// The tool drawings (#1120): the tool, holder and profile previews,
+    /// the library thumbnails, the tool body page, and the refusal and
+    /// warning inks of the tool pages. The previews keep their own dark
+    /// ground in both tables, as before.
+    pub tool_ground: Color32,
+    pub tool_axis: Color32,
+    pub tool_grid: Color32,
+    pub tool_flute: Color32,
+    pub tool_shank: Color32,
+    pub tool_body: Color32,
+    pub tool_edge: Color32,
+    pub tool_holder: Color32,
+    pub tool_note: Color32,
+    pub tool_dim: Color32,
+    pub thumb_flute: Color32,
+    pub bad_ink: Color32,
+    pub warn_ink: Color32,
+    pub mount_axis: Color32,
+    pub mount_radial: Color32,
+    pub mount_tip: Color32,
+    pub mount_origin: Color32,
+    pub mount_hint: Color32,
+    /// A floating window's close button: its hover fill and the cross on it.
+    pub close_hover: Color32,
+    pub close_ink: Color32,
+    // -- geometry: the Phase-6 complaint made themeable - ribbon size,
+    // input fields and button size are tokens, not literals.
+    /// Corner radius of widget rects and painted cells/rows.
+    pub radius_widget: u8,
+    /// Corner radius of egui windows.
+    pub radius_window: u8,
+    /// Corner radius of menus and combo dropdowns.
+    pub radius_menu: u8,
+    /// egui item spacing, x/y.
+    pub item_spacing_x: f32,
+    pub item_spacing_y: f32,
+    /// egui button padding, x/y.
+    pub button_padding_x: f32,
+    pub button_padding_y: f32,
+    /// Input-field/combo minimum height (egui's `interact_size.y`).
+    pub control_height: f32,
+    /// Browser tree row height (painted::tree).
+    pub row_height: f32,
+    /// Ribbon cell height (painted cell box; RIBBON_H follows it).
+    pub cell_h: f32,
+    /// Ribbon cell width cap (panes' flow clamp; floor is geometry).
+    pub cell_w: f32,
+    /// Ribbon glyph edge (the PNG and the painted fallback ride it).
+    pub glyph_px: f32,
+    /// Cell caption size under the ribbon glyph.
+    pub font_label: f32,
+    /// Group caption size.
+    pub font_caption: f32,
+    /// Browser row label size.
+    pub font_row: f32,
+    /// Browser row suffix size.
+    pub font_row_suffix: f32,
+    /// Ribbon rows (#2021): the tab row, then the gap to the cells.
+    pub ribbon_tab_h: f32,
+    pub ribbon_cell_top_gap: f32,
+    /// Gap from the cell box to the caption row, the row, the bottom gap.
+    pub ribbon_caption_gap: f32,
+    pub ribbon_caption_row_h: f32,
+    pub ribbon_bottom_gap: f32,
+    /// Shell metrics (#2064): window inner margin, status strip height, and
+    /// ribbon tab horizontal padding, gap and active underline thickness.
+    pub window_margin: f32,
+    pub status_h: f32,
+    pub ribbon_tab_pad_x: f32,
+    pub ribbon_tab_gap: f32,
+    pub ribbon_tab_stroke: f32,
+    /// Minimum point size when shrinking an overflowing ribbon cell label.
+    pub font_label_min: f32,
+    /// Operation tab strip (#2066): row height, inner horizontal pad, inter-tab gap, bottom gap.
+    pub op_tab_h: f32,
+    pub op_tab_pad_x: f32,
+    pub op_tab_gap: f32,
+    pub op_tab_bottom_gap: f32,
+    /// Operation tab icon edge, icon-to-label gap, top corner radius and font size.
+    pub op_tab_icon_px: f32,
+    pub op_tab_icon_gap: f32,
+    pub op_tab_radius: u8,
+    pub font_op_tab: f32,
+    /// Browser tree & pane (#2066): glyph edge, root left inset, per-depth indent.
+    pub tree_glyph_px: f32,
+    pub tree_inset_x: f32,
+    pub tree_indent: f32,
+    /// Eye reserve width, header/row pad x/y, label-to-suffix gap, header font boost.
+    pub tree_eye_reserve: f32,
+    pub tree_pad_x: f32,
+    pub tree_pad_y: f32,
+    pub tree_suffix_gap: f32,
+    pub tree_header_boost: f32,
+    /// Active rule / row highlight / drop-target stroke thickness (px).
+    pub highlight_stroke_px: f32,
+    /// Dropdown width, recent-list width, trigger gap and row inset in points (#2065).
+    pub menu_width: f32,
+    pub recent_width: f32,
+    pub menu_gap: f32,
+    pub menu_pad_x: f32,
+}
+
+/// The ribbon strip's height: the tab row, its gap, the cell box, the
+/// caption gap, the caption row and the bottom gap, all from the theme
+/// (88 at the built-in tables). A theme that grows a row grows the ribbon.
+#[must_use]
+pub const fn ribbon_h(t: &Tokens) -> f32 {
+    t.ribbon_tab_h
+        + t.ribbon_cell_top_gap
+        + t.cell_h
+        + t.ribbon_caption_gap
+        + t.ribbon_caption_row_h
+        + t.ribbon_bottom_gap
+}
+
+/// Bottom status strip height (px), tracking typography and controls (#2064).
+#[must_use]
+pub const fn status_h(t: &Tokens) -> f32 {
+    let a = if t.control_height + 4.0 > t.status_h { t.control_height + 4.0 } else { t.status_h };
+    if t.font_row * 1.3 + 4.0 > a { t.font_row * 1.3 + 4.0 } else { a }
+}
+
+impl Tokens {
+    /// Validated popup widths and row spacing shared by every dropdown.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn dropdown(&self) -> DropGeom {
+        DropGeom::from_tokens(self)
+    }
+
+    /// The panel ground behind the ribbon/browser strips (painted.rs).
+    #[must_use]
+    pub const fn strip_fill(&self) -> Color32 {
+        self.ink_alt
+    }
+
+    /// Build the egui Visuals from the tokens: every default-egui colour
+    /// and corner the shell shows is named here, so the widget path and
+    /// the painted path cannot disagree about what the theme is.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn visuals(&self) -> Visuals {
+        // The destructuring arm: every COLOUR is named here and nowhere
+        // else; a new colour field without a wiring line is a build
+        // error, not default-egui grey. (Geometry routes through
+        // `style()`; the const guard below covers those names.)
+        let Tokens {
+            ink, ink_alt, well, text, text_dim, text_faint, border, accent,
+            accent_hover, field_bg, field_hover, field_active, selection_bg,
+            selection_stroke, viewport: _, ribbon_ink: _,
+            handle_shade: _, handle_text: _, pick_rim: _,
+            cube_edge: _, cube_label: _, cube_glyph_on: _, cube_glyph_off: _, viewport_hint: _, marker_stem: _, marker_ring: _, marker_dot: _, axis_x: _, axis_y: _, axis_z: _, viewport_hover: _,
+            overlay_panel: _, overlay_edge: _, overlay_text: _, overlay_track: _, drop_veil: _, empty_hint: _, pick_halo: _, plate_hole: _, plate_dowel: _, gcode_line: _,
+            tool_ground: _, tool_axis: _, tool_grid: _, tool_flute: _, tool_shank: _, tool_body: _, tool_edge: _, tool_holder: _, tool_note: _, tool_dim: _, thumb_flute: _, bad_ink: _, warn_ink: _, mount_axis: _, mount_radial: _, mount_tip: _, mount_origin: _, mount_hint: _,
+            close_hover: _, close_ink: _,
+            radius_widget, radius_window, radius_menu,
+            item_spacing_x: _, item_spacing_y: _,
+            button_padding_x: _, button_padding_y: _,
+            control_height: _, row_height: _, cell_h: _, cell_w: _,
+            glyph_px: _, font_label: _, font_caption: _,
+            font_row: _, font_row_suffix: _, ribbon_tab_h: _,
+            ribbon_cell_top_gap: _, ribbon_caption_gap: _,
+            ribbon_caption_row_h: _, ribbon_bottom_gap: _,
+            window_margin: _, status_h: _, ribbon_tab_pad_x: _,
+            ribbon_tab_gap: _, ribbon_tab_stroke: _,
+            font_label_min: _, op_tab_h: _, op_tab_pad_x: _, op_tab_gap: _,
+            op_tab_bottom_gap: _, op_tab_icon_px: _, op_tab_icon_gap: _,
+            op_tab_radius: _, font_op_tab: _, tree_glyph_px: _, tree_inset_x: _,
+            tree_indent: _, tree_eye_reserve: _, tree_pad_x: _, tree_pad_y: _,
+            tree_suffix_gap: _, tree_header_boost: _, highlight_stroke_px: _,
+            menu_width: _, recent_width: _, menu_gap: _, menu_pad_x: _,
+        } = *self;
+        let mut v = Visuals::dark();
+        v.panel_fill = ink;

+## #4394 - The UI kit crate `camcraft-ui-kit` and the edge `ui -> ui-kit`
+
+**What was decided.** A new crate `crates/ui-kit` (`camcraft-ui-kit`)
+holds the design system of the shell. This PR moves three things into
+it, unchanged in behaviour:
+
+- the theme token table `Tokens` with its two built-in columns, its
+  clamps (`theme::clamp`), its exhaustiveness guard, `DropGeom`,
+  `ribbon_h`, `status_h`, `Tokens::visuals`, `Tokens::style` and
+  `apply_to`;
+- the `camcraft-theme/1` reader (`theme_files`: `Theme`, `Cache`, `load`,
+  `discover`, `parse_text`, the caps, `COLOR_NAMES`, `GEOM_NAMES`);
+- the contrast arithmetic (`contrast`: `luma`, `ratio`, `on_fill`,
+  `follow`, `follow_states`, `readable`, `BODY`, `UI`) and
+  `light_ground`, which moved from `ground_ink` because the visuals and
+  the file overlay both call it.
+
+The kit depends on `egui` (the workspace pin `=0.36.2`) and
+`serde_json` only. It has no `camcraft-*` dependency. The optional
+feature `gallery` adds `eframe` (same pin) for the gallery window
+`ui-kit-gallery`; tests do not build it.
+
+`camcraft-ui` gets the new edge `camcraft-ui-kit`. It keeps the old
+module paths as re-exports (`egui_app::contrast`, `egui_app::theme`,
+`egui_app::theme_files`, `ground_ink::light_ground`), so no other file
+of the crate changes, and open UI PRs keep compiling.
+
+**Imported items (the edge `ui -> ui-kit`).** `camcraft-ui` uses about
+thirty items of the kit: `Tokens` (with `DARK`, `LIGHT`, `visuals`,
+`style`, `dropdown`, `strip_fill`), `apply_to`, `ribbon_h`, `status_h`,
+`DropGeom`, the `clamp` module and its ranges, the nine `contrast`
+items above, and the `theme_files` items above plus `ThemeSource` and
+`resolve_source`. That is far above the five-item floor of AGENTS.md.
+
+**Why the caller cannot pass the values in.** These items are not values
+that a caller could hand over as a parameter or a closure. They are the
+types and the functions that every draw site of the shell reads: the
+token table is the type of the theme itself. The maintainer asked for
+the UI/UX work in a crate, "one crate for the design system only
+(tokens, theme and components)" (#4245, 2026-11-27). The edge is the
+point of the change: the dependency graph now proves that the design
+system cannot read the document, because the kit cannot see
+`camcraft-app`.
+
+**What stays in `camcraft-ui`, and why.**
+
+- The live theme cell (`theme::current`, `theme::set_current`,
+  `theme::apply`) and its tests. Its unit-test form is a thread-local
+  (#2373), chosen by `#[cfg(test)]`. That `cfg` applies per crate: in the
+  kit it would be off while `camcraft-ui` runs its tests, and parallel
+  UI harness threads would share one theme again. The cell is shell
+  state, not design system, so it stays where the shell runs.
+- The map from the document's `ThemeRef` to the kit's `ThemeSource`
+  (`theme_files::resolve`). The kit has its own small enum, so it does
+  not need `camcraft-app`.
+
+**What rebuilds when the kit changes.** `camcraft-ui-kit` and
+`camcraft-ui` (its lib, its binary and its test binaries). No other
+crate depends on either, so a kit change rebuilds no engine crate, no
+`camcraft-app` and no flecs. A change in `camcraft-ui` does not rebuild
+the kit. `cargo test -p camcraft-ui-kit` builds egui and serde_json
+only.
+
+**Tests.** The four contrast tests moved from
+`crates/ui/tests/theme_files.rs` to `crates/ui-kit/tests/contrast.rs`
+unchanged. The kit adds `tests/gallery.rs` (four tests). `camcraft-ui`
+adds four tests for the seam (`egui_app/theme_files/resolve_tests.rs`:
+the `ThemeRef` map and the old paths), so its test count stays the same. The colour-literal guard of `camcraft-ui` loses the rows of
+`contrast.rs` and `theme/tables.rs`, because those files are no longer
+in that crate.
+
+**Gate.** The gate has fixed crate lists (`xtask/src/plan.rs`:
+`ALL_CRATES`, `BATCH_CRATES`, `CLIPPY`); it does not discover crates.
+Without an entry, a diff in `crates/ui-kit` would select no test and no
+clippy run. The PR adds `ui-kit` to the three lists, before `ui`
+(dependency order). This is a process file change.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- Move the live cell into the kit behind a feature that `camcraft-ui`
+  turns on as a dev-dependency. Dropped: Cargo unifies the feature for
+  all test targets of `camcraft-ui`, so its integration tests would
+  change from one process-wide theme to a thread-local one. That is a
+  behaviour change in a PR that must have none.
+- Move the layout widgets, the ribbon cell and the icons now (research
+  note 2 on #4245). Dropped: the issue asks for no big move. Later PRs
+  move each component in the PR that touches it.
+- Keep `ThemeRef` in the kit's signature. Dropped: it needs
+  `camcraft-app`, which the kit must never see.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small. The re-exports in `camcraft-ui` can go
+when the last caller uses the kit paths directly; that is a mechanical
+path change. Removing the crate again means moving the files back and
+deleting the edge.
